paras: The Yorkville whipping-party shooting was the accidental killing of Alex. Terrell near Yorkville, Gibson County, Tennessee, on a Sunday night in early April 1882, when, according to one report, a group of "boys" had gone out to whip a Black man. Terrell was shot in the neck and killed by Charles King, and no whipping is reported to have been carried out. Three Tennessee papers noted the death, but only the Rugbeian mentioned the whipping errand.

According to the Milan Exchange, a Gibson County paper, Charles King "accidentally shot in the neck Alex. Terrell, killing him instantly" near Yorkville on the Sunday night before its issue of April 8, 1882. The editor said he had heard "two or three stories about the affair, but nothing definite beyond the fact of the killing." A week later the Rugbeian, in its column of Tennessee news, added that "some boys had gone out for the purpose of whipping a negro when the accident happened," a detail it introduced with "We learn." Neither the intended target nor the members of the party other than Terrell and King are named, and the race of the party is not stated.
No report of an inquest, arrest or prosecution appears in the coverage, and nothing further is reported about the man the party had meant to whip.

The Milan Exchange ran the story under the heading "Fatally Shot" and treated it as "another fatal result of the pernicious custom of pistol carrying," without mentioning a whipping or any Black person. The Rugbeian, published at Rugby in Morgan County, placed the whipping errand in a one-sentence aside among other state briefs and offered no comment on it. The Memphis Daily Appeal of April 18 reduced the affair to a single line, saying Terrell had been killed "by the awkward handling of a pistol by Ch. King." No Black-press coverage is available for this period.

reader.title: Yorkville whipping-party shooting
bases: The only racial element is a single report that 'some boys' had set out to whip an unnamed Black man when one of their own party was accidentally shot (A2); no whipping, threat or contact with the intended target is reported, and the local paper and the Memphis Appeal describe only an accidental shooting (A1, A3).

The accidental killing of Alex. Terrell is corroborated by three papers (A1, A2, A3), but the planned whipping of a Black man, the only racial-violence element, appears only in the Rugbeian's 'We learn' item (A2).
